title: Wren and the Inheritance
premise: Estate lawyer Ines Fairweather is hired by a dying stranger, Wren Halloway, to prove that a murder listed in a thirty-year-old will never happened — because the will leaves everything to the victim, and if she's alive, someone has been living under her name. Ines traces the alibis of four witnesses who swore they saw the body, discovering each was paid to lie by the estate's executor. The victim, Ada, faked her death to escape an abusive marriage but lost her memory in the escape; she is Wren herself, unknowingly testifying against her own past. At the climax, Ines forces the executor's confession before witnesses, restoring Ada's name and inheritance — not through the courts, which failed her once, but through truth spoken aloud among the found family she built while hiding.
about_author: Jonah Oyelaran is a former court clerk from Lagos who now writes mysteries about paperwork, secrets, and the people who fall between legal cracks. He believes every file cabinet holds at least one ghost.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ines Fairweather, POV. A frail client named Wren pays triple retainer to prove a 1994 murder never occurred, producing a will that names the victim as sole heir. Ines, who prides themselves on closable cases, accepts despite the absurdity. Reading the old police file, they find four witnesses with suspiciously identical phrasing. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Four Alibis, One Inkwell
chapters.summary: Ines POV, alternating with Wren's fragmented memories. Ines interviews the aging witnesses; each alibi collapses under small contradictions, and all were paid by executor Marcus Vane. Meanwhile Wren recalls a burning house and a river, unsure whose memories they are. Emotional beat: dread deepening as the conspiracy reveals itself, and tenderness growing between lawyer and client.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Following the river trail, Ines finds a boathouse, a hidden identity kit, and proof that 'Wren' is Ada herself — amnesiac survivor of her own staged death. Confronting Vane privately, Ines is threatened: expose him and Ada's fragile new life shatters too. Emotional beat: betrayal and heartbreak — winning the case may destroy the client.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ines and Wren/Ada POV together. Rather than courts, Ines gathers the four witnesses and Vane at the estate, reading the will aloud and letting Ada's recovered memories confront each liar in turn until Vane confesses before everyone. Ada reclaims her name; the witnesses, complicit but remorseful, become her chosen family. Emotional beat: catharsis — justice outside the law, and a self inherited whole.
